content.html:
datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages

I was looking at the Firefox network panel today when I noticed that requests to a Datasette table page were triggering anHTTP prefetch to the next page of rows in that table.

This was happening because Datasette pages serve an HTTPlinkheader like this:

link: <https://latest.datasette.io/fixtures/compound_three_primary_keys?_next=a%2Cd%2Cv>; rel="next"

This is bad. A tiny fraction of the visitors to one of those pages will click the "next" link, which means their browser is fetching unnecessary data and the Datasette server is having to render an entire page that then gets thrown away.

I dug in and learned that Firefox hasan issuethat has been open for 24 years about this behavior...

And one of the early comments on that issue links tomy blog post from 2002complaining about this feature. I hadn't just forgotten that I had written about it, I had forgotten the feature entirely!

content.html:
Afterweeks of backlash—anda failed attempt to quell it—Meta has indefinitely delayed plans to update its commercial terms and require Meta Business account users to allow extensive AI training on external websites linked on Facebook.

"We're pausing the ‌changes ⁠as we continue to engage with stakeholders and ​take ​our ⁠time to get this right. ​In the ​meantime, ⁠our existing terms remain in ⁠effect," a Meta spokespersontold Reuters.

Soon after Meta notified business account holders of the upcoming changes, legal experts warned Nieman Lab that the vague language could allow the company to ignore scraping preferences specified in robots.txt files and exhaustively crawl vast amounts of off-Facebook content for AI training. Since virtually every news publisher has a Facebook page, Nieman Lab sounded the alarm that Meta could potentially avoid millions in licensing fees if the TOS update happened as planned.

六张卡跑同一个 MiniMax-H3 视频工作流，差多少？

4090 单条耗电最低（10.3 Wh），但速度不是最快。

按「每瓦出片量」算，5090 和 4090 接近（速度更快但功耗高），

170HX 用 226 W 就跑完虽然慢，能耗只比 5090 高 21%，能耗表现不错。

两张 7900 XTX 的能效最差——TP2 的通信开销和单卡的软件栈低效让它们耗电是 4090 的 3.5 倍。

一个反直觉的发现：16 GB 能跑，24 GB 反而 OOM

RTX 5080 只有 16 GB，15 秒能跑完（665 s）。

7900 XTX 有 24 GB，15 秒直接CUDA out of memory。

查下来原因不是容量，是能不能动态换页：

项目RTX 5080（16 GB 能跑）7900 XTX（24 GB 不能跑）
comfy-aimdo动态卸载有无
20 GB 权重的处理Staged 到系统内存，按需流式送入显存必须全部常驻显存
显存峰值15.21 GB（恒定满，持续换页）23.98 GB（撑死）
系统内存参与峰值 30.6 GB，起关键作用不参与卸载

NVIDIA 的comfy-aimdo把显存变成了「缓存」而不是「仓库」，所以 16 GB 够用。

AMD ROCm 缺这套机制，24 GB 是必须同时装下权重 + 激活的硬门槛。

试过但无效的修法：PYTORCH_HIP_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True

碎片从 5.57 GB 降到 2.27 GB（确实生效），但总占用涨到 21.26 GB，还是差 1.19 GB。

所以是硬性容量不足，不是碎片问题。

结论

  1. 要速度→ RTX 5090（5 秒 75 s），三档全部领先
  2. 要能效→ RTX 4090（单条 10.3 Wh 最低）或 5090（11.3 Wh 但快 15%）
  3. 要长视频→ 5090 或 170HX，显存余量足
  4. 不推荐7900 XTX 双卡 TP2：15 秒 1460 s 比 170HX 单卡还慢
  5. 降功耗策略：5080 可以压到 60%（只慢 4%）；4090 压到 85% 划算（省 14% 电只慢 4.5%），压到 60% 慢 42% 就不值了

其实我对Radiance项目的理解很肤浅。很多的情况是基于我跟AI聊天所获得的信息。尽管参与过对Radiance在7900XTX平台上的移植，但当时只是单纯觉得实现TP=2就是实现了复刻移植。

直到昨天，听了老特对Radiance项目拆解介绍，我攸有种顿悟的感觉。
https://lcz.me/topic/2826

客观讲，Radiance项目最大的收益来自于TP=2的系列优化，这没错。但是不能说实现了TP=2就复刻了 Radiance这个项目。

简单说，TP=2只是实现了把单车道拓成双车道，但Radiance的本质，更接近于双车道的红绿灯系统+交警管制。如果能更好的调整通道，是不是可以在TP=2的基础上进一步提升效率，不断地逼进帕累托最优状态？这是我的猜想，这也是进一步要验证的。

成果还是挺让我惊喜的：
在视频生成范畴，在大分辨率，长视频生成过程中，累加TP=2的最大优化最多可以节约18.8%的生成时间，重要的是没有代价，无痛提升。

本项目的参数相对温和，调参至激进策略需要牺牲一部分画质，在此基础上仍有20%~25%的加速空间。

在拆解的过程中发现Radiance确实是个很优秀的项目，目前本项目对照Radiance仍优化空间。之后的优化对象难度较大，需要时间，项目分持续更新。（详见文件第6部分）

项目名称不是耍宝，整体的思路就是通过平A的组合换得一个大招。这跟《浪客剑心》中比古清十郎教授的九头龙闪，简直异曲同工。

这个项目中，单个项目MLP 分块、VAE 跨卡、心跳兜底、帧计划对账优化收益微小，甚至无收益。但放在整个项目组合后放大，甚至取得非线性收益（如VAE拆分）。

同时也致敬我非常喜欢的动漫作品《浪客剑心》。

-------------------------祖传手打分割线--------------------------

Kuzuryūsen · 九頭龍閃

把 H3 视频生成在两张卡上拆成两条并行流水：采样阶段把 MLP 切块、让 all_reduce 与 GEMM 在独立流上重叠；出片阶段把 VAE 解码按模型自带的时间块分给两卡，再用点对点交换接缝帧。8 步 832×480 / 124 帧实测：出片 34.0 → 28.5 s，采样 8.810 → 7.616 s/step，端到端 152 → 132 s（−13%），像素误差 0。

这是相对「你原先的优化」的增量：TP2 与 P2P 已实现，今天只叠加 MLP 分块 + VAE 跨卡。

2.0 适用对象

适用

  • 已上或准备上 TP=2 的双卡生产环境（单卡不在收益范围，见 §4）。

  • 出片段占比高的视频工作流：H3 / MiniMax 类 DiT 视频模型，VAE 解码 + CPU 帧转换合计占 post 六成以上。

  • 批量出片：一次加载连续跑多条，固定约 48 s 的开销被摊薄，1080p 以上总优化约 18%。

  • 显存吃紧的 24 GB AMD 卡（7900 XTX，已实测）：单卡放不下整片解码，需要按时间块把 VAE 分摊到两卡。

  • 对画质有硬要求、不能接受 int8 或近似算法，但愿意重构编排的团队。

content.html:
This October, GitHub saw more than 1.2 billion commits in one week—over 400% more than a year earlier. This is more commits than GitHub received in all of 2025. Chances are, you’re generating more code than you were a year ago. But ask yourself: do you feel 400% more productive than you were last year?

Building software takes more than a good prompt. As AI speeds up implementation, software developers are feeling more pressure in other places:a Faros AI studyfound that pull requests spent 441% longer in review when teams went from low to high AI adoption.

As a software developer, you gather requirements and steer implementation, review changes and evaluate test results, then investigate what happens in production. Agents can help you work more efficiently across all of these stages: Plan, Build, Verify, and Observe. We’ll walk through what an effective agentic engineering workflow looks like on GitHub.

Plan: Get everyone and every agent on the same page

See if this sounds familiar. You’re planning an API change. The design is in one tool, a compatibility requirement is buried in Slack, and an old pull request explains why the current implementation works this way. Before you can write a useful plan, you need to connect those details, compare approaches, and agree on how existing clients will keep working. What looked like a straightforward planning task has become hours of searching, cross-checking, and chasing answers. You’re exhausted before implementation even begins.

You can use Copilot to pull that scattered context into one place, work through the tradeoffs, and turn the decisions into an implementation plan.

  • Plan together where your team already works.UseCopilot in Slack or Teamsto collaborate with everyone involved—from product managers and designers to analysts and business stakeholders. Bring in context from connected tools so your team can check assumptions, contribute ideas, and refine requirements together.
  • Turn agreed-upon requirements into actionable work.Ask Copilot tocreate GitHub Issueswith the context and acceptance criteria needed for implementation, breaking out tasks that can be handled separately.
  • Keep routine triage from consuming planning time.UseGitHub Agentic Workflowsto label your issues and estimate task complexity. Assign low-complexity tasks directly to Copilot, then spend your time focusing on harder decisions.
  • Give complex work the planning it needs.UsePlan Modein your preferred Copilot surface to compare approaches and refine an implementation plan. Review and approve the plan before handing it off to Copilot to begin implementation.

What took days of searching and context gathering now produces a reviewable plan, explicit acceptance criteria, and scoped issues, with your time spent on the decisions instead of the retrieval. Then, once you settle on an approach, you’ve already set yourself and your agents up to implement your plan.

Build: Move more than one task forward at a time

You’re ready to turn that plan into code. But life has other ideas. Your agent is halfway through a task, your next meeting starts in five minutes, and your dog has been staring at the door for twenty. Then someone in the meeting points out an edge case the implementation needs to handle. Everyone needs something from you at once. You’d like to keep making progress, but you can’t be in three places at the same time.

content.html:
Most of the changes I make to my projects these days come in the form of PRs opened for me by Claude Code or Codex. The PR is my unit of work - I use them to bundle commits together, iterating on them until a feature is complete, document decisions and then merge the finished result. Today's coding agents are great at writing PR descriptions.

They're too good at describing the work

The problem is that they aretoogood. An agent-written PR description is accurate and comprehensive. It describes the problem, the detailed solution, and the steps taken to verify it. That's a lot of information to absorb.

It's not necessarily slop, but itreadslike slop!

It's very easy to spot an AI-written PR, and as with other forms of AI writing my instant reaction is best summarized as "I'm not reading all of that". It doesn't matter how accurate or useful the information is, I'm instantly put off by the thought that it will take me longer to read than it took the driving author to write... even when that driving author is me!

I want human editorial judgement. I want someone to have thought just long enough about the PR to give me a human-approved introduction that helps me understand, at a high level, what the PR is for and whether it deserves more of my attention.

I think I've found a low-effort way to do this that feels right.

Hide most of it in a details/summary

The HTML<details><summary>elements render as a collapsed heading (the summary) that can be expanded to view the larger piece of text. The code looks like this:

<details><summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary><h2>The hook</h2>Plugins implement<code>register_agent_reference_types(datasette)</code>...</details>

When rendered, it lookslike this:

Crucially,<details><summary>is supported in GitHub Markdown. You can drop those tags directly into an issue comment or PR description and GitHub will hide the details and display just the summary plus an expansion arrow.

I've started using this for my AI-generated pull requests.

The opening paragraph of my PRs will be carefully selected to act as a high-level explanation of what's going on - the shortest text a human can read that will help get them up to speed.

I'll sometimes throw in a screenshot as well, since images are often the best way to quickly illustrate a new feature.

The full agent-written essay then follows in a<details><summary>. I use the model name and often the effort level as that summary, to make it abundantly clear what is going on - "Claude Opus 5.5 Medium" for example.

My PRs don't feel nearly as sloppy now! The information is all still there, but a reader can glance at it and get the top, human-curated information without their eyes glazing over at multiple paragraphs of agent-written details.

I don't always write the introduction myself - sometimes the agent has given me what I need already, hidden away in the avalanche of other text. My promise to the reader is that the short opener will represent my human judgement as to what is definitely worth their time.

Here are some recent examples where I've used this pattern, including the opener I used:

  • datasette PR #3052: Redesign row page as a vertical list of fields- "The row page showed its single row as a one-row table. For wide tables, like a 46-column GitHubrepostable, that scrolled far off to the right and left most of the page blank." (then a screenshot)
  • datasette PR #3043: Pagination bar showing which rows are on the current page- "Table pages that span more than one page now make it obvious where you are, and offer navigation at the top of the page as well as the bottom." (plus screenshot)
  • datasette PR #3042: Load edit-tools.js on demand via a small loader- "edit-tools.js(~220KB) was loaded on every table, row and database page, even for users who couldn't edit anything. Now only load it for users who can edit when they first interact with an edit feature (including mouse over an edit link)."
  • datasette-agent PR #51: register_agent_reference_types plugin hook- "Lets plugins add their own kinds of item to the#tagging in the chat composer using a newregister_agent_reference_types(datasette)plugin hook." - pictured above.
  • llm PR #1838: Add llm openai endpoint add/list/remove/path commands- "Adds commands for managing the records inextra-openai-models.yaml, so OpenAI-compatible endpoints can be saved from the command line instead of by hand-editing YAML." - then copied--helpoutput.

content.html:
Research:parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust

I was out walking the dog when I got curious about how easy/difficult it would be to write a SQLite C extension that adds aparse_number()function for turning strings like-$1,234.56or'12.5%'into numeric values that could be summed and sorted.

I fired up regular Claude chat (Opus 5.5)and prompted:

I'm thinking about a SQLite custom function 'parse_number(value)' that strips ',', '$', '£' and '%', handles a leading '-', and returns 'NULL' for anything it can’t parse

Explore the difference between building this as a SQLite extension in C v.s. in Rust - I want to compare performance and code complexity and size of the resulting.so(or whatever) file

This gave me a solid starting point - the Rust extension was 321 KB (usingRusqlite) and 298 KB (usingsqlite-loadable-rs), while the C extension was 14 KB. But the Rust extension was faster!

Turns out that's because the Rust equivalent of C'sstrtodis "twice as fast". So I prompted:

Try writing your own C function for parsing text into a decimal number that catches up to or beats the Rust implementation

And it did:

Mixed data67 ns19 ns46 ns41 ns
Integers only25 ns16 ns36 ns32 ns
Decimals only106 ns18 ns55 ns47 ns

Clone simonw/research from GitHub and turn your above investigation into a research report as seen in that repository - you can give me a zip file to download that contains your new folder

Here'sthe resulting report.

Basalt 是 Strata 的 fork，改动集中在 CPU 调度层：更细的 row-range 任务切分、i-quant 走 AVX-VNNI、单文件 .basalt 格式。社区里常见 2 倍的说法，所以拿同机同模型做了对比。

结论：确实更快，但没有 2 倍，实测 1.26 到 1.42 倍。

一、前后对比

同一台机器、同一个模型（Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS）、同一张卡（250 W 锁功耗），basalt-bench 固定 seed：

指标Strata 0.2.9Basalt 0.3.0倍率
prefill 64K1960 tok/s2725 tok/s1.39
decode（MTP 接受率 65-70%）58 tok/s73 tok/s1.26
decode（接受率 97-98%）104 tok/s148 tok/s1.42

decode 的差异主要来自 MTP 接受率：接受率高时窗口里挤进更多 token，固定开销被摊薄。两个引擎都是这个规律。

二、为什么不是 2 倍

社区里 2 倍的数据基本出自 5 GHz、带 AVX-VNNI 的桌面 CPU（9950X、285K 之类）。这台是 Xeon Gold 6252，2019 年的 Cascade Lake，2.1 GHz。

从三个 fixture 反推窗口开销，能拟合出：每个 decode 窗口约 19 ms 固定 + 4.1 ms/token。48 层摊下来每层约 0.4 ms，花在 CPU 侧串行的专家点积和主机与卡之间的握手上，不在显卡算力。

几个直接证据：

  • 引擎启动日志自己写了：this CPU has no AVX-512: the expert kernels run on AVX-2。这颗 U 有 AVX512-VNNI，但缺 VBMI/VBMI2，Basalt 判定不可用退回 AVX2；而 AVX-VNNI（VEX 版）它也没有，恰好是 Basalt 重点优化的那条路。
  • 把显存里的专家数从 6.7 GiB（Strata）提到 13.3 GiB（Basalt），翻了一倍，速度只涨 1.2 到 1.4 倍。瓶颈不在显存。
  • basalt-bench --hardware实测：RAM 读 48.6 GB/s，PCIe 3.0 x16、H2D 13.8 GB/s。宿主链路 LnkCap 支持 32 GT/s，LnkSta 只跑 8 GT/s，因为 6252 平台本身就是 PCIe 3.0。
  • 内存拓扑更隐蔽：宿主 node0 有 46.9 GB（带核），node1 有 48.3 GB 但没有核。虚拟机 74 GiB 必然跨两个节点，约一半内存每次访问都要过跨节点链路。

所以这台机器上是两个引擎同时撞同一堵墙：Strata 慢是因为墙，Basalt 也只快在墙内能优化的那部分。

三、容器化，损失多少

原来是裸进程（systemd），现在跑容器：

  • 镜像basalt-5070ti-256k-img:latest，3.05 GB，基于nvidia/cuda:13.0.0-runtime-ubuntu24.04，只装 python3、jinja2、regex、numpy。
  • 权重只读挂载，配置只读挂载，状态目录可写。

同口径基准：

指标裸进程容器差值
prefill 64K27252648-2.8%
decode conv73720%
decode struct148151+2%
decode prose72720%

基本在噪声里。关键是三个参数别省：--ulimit memlock=-1（否则专家页锁失败退回文件映射，速度直接掉）、--shm-size给够、不要设 CPU 配额。

四、预热和跨对话缓存

容器入口脚本会在模型加载完后自动预热 23 秒：DSH 的系统提示词（7.3K token）、Hermes 的提示词（0.8K）、一段 300 字生成、一张图（识图路径）。都是为了把专家缓存和 MTP 状态跑热。

效果是数量级的：

同一个 2 万 token 提示词，冷启动 31.5 秒，预热后 7.1 秒。这解释了「刚启动那几轮为什么慢」——不是配置坏了。

第二层是会话检查点：离开再回到同一个对话，日志里是restored 13037 tokens (checkpoint) in 65.4 ms，同一提示词从 4.3 秒掉到 90 毫秒。

第三层是磁盘停放：容器重启后照样能读回，read 13037 tokens from disk in 457.4 ms。实测快照约 8.1 KB/token，一个 19.5 万 token 的会话落盘 1.5 GiB，32 GiB 预算大概放得下 20 个 20 万 token 的会话。

五、配置与启动

{
"version": 2,
"models": [{
"model": "/models/Qwen3.8-FN-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS.basalt",
"alias": "5070Ti-QFNext-iQ3xxs-Basalt",
"gpu": "0",
"max-context": 262144,
"kv": "int8",
"vision": "dynamic"
}],
"engine": {
"resident-experts": true,
"vram-reserve-mib": 256,
"spec": 8,
"expert-profile-save": "/state/expert-profile-learned.bin",
"conversation-cache-mib": 2048,
"conversation-cache-slots": 4,
"conversation-cache-min-tokens": 8192,
"conversation-cache-disk-mib": 32768,
"conversation-cache-dir": "/state/conversations"
},
"server": { "host": "0.0.0.0", "port": 8030 }
}

启动：

docker run -d --name Basalt-5070ti-256K-img \
--gpus "device=0" \
--ulimit memlock=-1 \
--shm-size=2g \
-p 8030:8030 \
-v /data/aimodels/basalt:/models:ro \
-v /data/basalt-state:/state \
-v /data/basalt-state/warmup:/warmup:ro \
-v /path/basalt_config.json:/config.json:ro \
--restart unless-stopped \
basalt-5070ti-256k-img:latest

加载 43.8 GiB（显存 13.0 + 内存 30.8），冷启动约 85 秒，262144 上下文可用，识图一张图 1 到 2 秒。

参数是实测筛过的，别照抄网上的：kv k8v4省 23% 的 KV 但 prefill 掉 7%；spec 4让结构化输出从 148 掉到 133；resident-budget-gib压到 26 GiB 会触发专家溢写到 SSD，prefill 直接腰斩。256K 上下文相对 66K 的 prefill 只差 0.2%，所以直接拉满。

content.html:
Avalon (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) Windows 部署文档

日期：2026-11-07
硬件：AMD RX 7900 XTX 24GB / Ryzen 5 5600G / DDR4 双通道（系统实际识别 63.4 GB）
项目：https://github.com/freriadoc/Avalon（llama.cpp 分支，专为 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B MoE 优化）
成果：Windows 下从零编译部署成功，实测生成 54–58 t/s（MTP，512 token）

一、最终部署布局

项路径 / 值
源码C:\AI\Avalon（git clone，main 分支）
可执行文件C:\AI\Avalon\build\bin\llama-server.exe
启动脚本C:\AI\Avalon\avalon-server.bat
模型C:\AI\models\Avalon-GGUF（91 GiB，33 分片 IQ3_KS + MTP + moe-cache-ranking.bin）
HIP SDKC:\Program Files\AMD\ROCm\7.2
编译脚本C:\AI\Avalon\build_windows.bat（首次）/build_only.bat（增量）
服务地址http://0.0.0.0:8080（OpenAI 兼容/v1/chat/completions）

️ 模型必须放在 NVMe SSD。放机械硬盘时生成仅 3–6 t/s，挪到 NVMe 后 49–58 t/s。模型里有个 36 GB 的 per-layer token embedding 张量每个 token 都要访问，HDD 随机读直接把速度打死。

二、环境准备

  1. Visual Studio 2026 Community（含 MSVC 14.51、CMake、Ninja）——VS 自带 CMake 路径：
    C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Community\Common7\IDE\CommonExtensions\Microsoft\CMake\{CMake\bin\cmake.exe, Ninja}
  2. AMD HIP SDK 7.2：官网下载页 → Windows 11 / 7.2，实际直链（1.6 GB）：
    https://download.amd.com/developer/eula/rocm-hub/AMD-Software-PRO-Edition-26.Q3-Win11-For-HIP.exe
    静默安装：Start-Process <exe> -ArgumentList '-install','-log','C:\AI\hip_install.log' -Verb RunAs -Wait（会弹 UAC）
  3. git，python 3.14 + huggingface_hub（pip install huggingface_hub，下载用hf.exe，位于%APPDATA%\Python\Python314\Scripts）
  4. 网络代理：本机127.0.0.1:7890可用（git/curl 走-x http://127.0.0.1:7890；GitHub 直连超时）

三、编译（关键坑与解法）

配置命令（在build_windows.bat内完成，需 vcvars64 环境）：

call "...\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat"
set HIP_PATH=C:\Program Files\AMD\ROCm\7.2
set CXXFLAGS=-isystem C:\AI\Avalon\hip_compat
cmake -B build -G Ninja -DGGML_HIP=ON -DAMDGPU_TARGETS=gfx1100 ^
-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++
cmake --build build --target llama-server -j 8

坑 1：MSVC 14.51<cmath>与 HIP clang 冲突（必须修）

错误形态：

error: __device__ function 'isgreater' cannot overload __host__ __device__ function 'isgreater'
（引用 MSVC 14.51 cmath 的 _CLANG_BUILTIN2(isgreater)）

原因：MSVC 14.51 起把isgreater/isless等声明为 constexpr（clang 下隐含__host__ __device__），与 ROCm clang 的__device__声明冲突。上游修复见 LLVM PR #201563、Strata PR #373。

解法（同 Strata 方案）：建垫片目录，并把CXXFLAGS=-isystem <垫片目录>加进环境：

// C:\AI\Avalon\hip_compat\cmath
#if defined(__HIP__)
#include <__clang_cuda_math_forward_declares.h>
#endif
#include_next <cmath>

注意：.bat里不要写中文注释（GBK 代码页下 UTF-8 中文会破坏 cmd 解析）。

坑 2：moe-cache.cuPOSIXclose()（必须修）

ggml/src/ggml-cuda/moe-cache.cu约 3647 行close(f.second)在 Windows 无此符号。修法：文件头部_WIN32块加#include <io.h>，该处改为：

#if defined(_WIN32)
_close(f.second);
#else
close(f.second);
#endif

其他

  • Ninja 不在 PATH：把上面 VS 的 Ninja 目录加进 PATH。
  • 直接clang链接失败（oldnames.lib找不到）：必须在 vcvars64 环境里跑 CMake。
  • 编译时长约 25 分钟（iGPU 6 核，283 个目标）。

四、模型下载

# 国内走 hf-mirror 更快；HuggingFace 官方源经代理实测会掉到 ~100KB/s
export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com
hf download freriadoc/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Avalon-GGUF --local-dir C:\AI\models\Avalon-GGUF
  • 39 个文件共 91 GiB，镜像实测 ~200MB/s、21 分钟下完；官方源经代理 3 小时仅 3 GB。
  • 校验目录：33 个Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-Avalon-IQ3KS-000xx-of-00033.gguf+MTP\mtp-...FR65k.gguf+moe-cache-ranking.bin。
  • 与 Strata 的 IQ3_S 模型不通用（Avalon 用自有 IQ3_KS 混合量化 + 专属张量布局），必须单独下载。

三、编译（关键坑与解法）
配置命令（在 build_windows.bat 内完成，需 vcvars64 环境）：

-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++

坑 1：MSVC 14.51 <cmath> 与 HIP clang 冲突（必须修）
错误形态：
error: __device__ function 'isgreater' cannot overload __host__ __device__ function 'isgreater'
（引用 MSVC 14.51 cmath 的 _CLANG_BUILTIN2(isgreater)）

// C:\AI\Avalon\hip_compat\cmath
#if defined(__HIP__)

#endif
#include_next <cmath>

#if defined(_WIN32)
_close(f.second);
#else
close(f.second);
#endif

直接 clang 链接失败（ oldnames.lib 找不到）：必须在 vcvars64 环境里跑 CMake。

content.html:
给 DGX Spark 写了个零依赖实时监控面板：1 个 Python 文件 + 1 个 HTML 文件

起因：在 DGX Spark 上跑大模型时，想随时看清 CPU / GPU / 统一内存 / 磁盘 / 网络 / 推理吞吐的真实状态，
以及推理引擎（推理服务）到底跑得怎么样。官方 Dashboard 看不了推理细节，nvtop/btop又看不到
LLM 侧的指标，索性自己写了一个。

约束：零第三方依赖——后端只用 Python 标准库，前端单文件 HTML + 原生 JS，不引任何 CDN。
拷过去python3 monitor.py就能跑。

[整体效果]

目录

  • 它有什么
  • 架构
  • 值得抄的 6 个实现细节
  • 部署
  • 踩坑清单
  • 文件清单
  • 已知限制

它有什么

17 个面板，全部可拖动、可缩放、可换位置，布局存在浏览器本地，导出一段 JSON 就能在别的机器上复现。

顶部 9 张 KPI 卡带迷你走势线；中间 6 张曲线图支持鼠标悬停出十字线和数值气泡，Y 轴单位会在
B/s → KB/s → MB/s之间自动切换。

[LLM 运维区]

上排是推理引擎（running/waiting、解码速度、TTFT、TPOT、KV Cache 分池占用、MTP 接受率）、
容器 llm（CPU / 内存 / net / block IO）、一键测速（发一次真实对话，按usage计数算吞吐）。

下排是硬件明细：CPU 每核负载（20 核 GB10）、温度传感器 / 风扇（带过热状态染色）、
磁盘 I/O、网络接口（含错误/丢包计数）。

[硬件表格区]

再往下是进程 Top、引擎指标明细表、当前生效配置（直接读容器里的环境变量，一眼看到
TF_SOLO_ROWS/TF_SPILL_GIB这些实际生效的参数）、容器日志尾部。

[进程 / 引擎指标 / 生效配置]

交互细节

鼠标悬停在曲线上，十字线定位到具体时刻，气泡给出该时刻的各序列数值：

[悬停交互]

拖卡片标题栏换位置，拖右下角的小三角改大小。布局可以导出成 JSON：

[布局导出]

复制这段 JSON，粘到另一台机器上点「应用」，就是一模一样的排布。

架构

monitor.py ~34 KB Python 3 标准库，无第三方依赖
├─ 采样线程 1 Hz 写环形缓冲（deque(maxlen=...)）
├─ HTTP 服务 ThreadingHTTPServer
└─ API
/api/snapshot 当前快照（含 host/cpu/memory/gpu/sensors/disk/network/processes/engine）
/api/series 历史序列，?window=60|300|900|1800|3600
/api/stats snapshot + 容器 stats + uptime
/api/config 容器镜像/状态/环境变量（docker inspect）
/api/logs 容器日志尾部 ?tail=200
/api/probe 发一次真实对话，测 TTFT / decode 速度
/api/key 设置 API Key
/api/healthz
index.html ~49 KB 单文件：HTML + CSS + JS，无 CDN

为什么服务端采样？因为磁盘/网络的速率本质上就是「两次采样之间的差值」，没法在 HTTP 请求发生的
那一刻凭空算出来。所以有一个后台线程固定 1 Hz 采样写进deque，前端只是来取。

值得抄的 6 个实现细节

1. 速率只能用 delta 算，不能在请求时重新采样

这是最容易踩的坑。直觉写法是「收到请求 → 读一次/proc/diskstats→ 和上次比」，但**「上次」存在哪**
是问题：如果请求比采样线程更频繁，就会拿两个几乎同时刻的采样点作差，差值被摊薄成一个极小的时间窗，
算出来的速率要么是 0，要么抖得没法看。

正确做法是：后台线程独占采样，HTTP 只返回缓存的结果。

def disk_info(prev, dt):
"""prev 是上一次采样的 /proc/diskstats 快照，dt 是两次采样之间的时间差。"""
for name, v in cur.items():
old = (prev or {}).get(name)
if old and dt > 0:
d["read_bps"] = round((v[2] - old[2]) * 512 / dt, 1) # 扇区数 × 512 = 字节
d["write_bps"] = round((v[6] - old[6]) * 512 / dt, 1)
d["read_iops"] = round((v[0] - old[0]) / dt, 2)

后台循环里dt用真实经过时间：

def sample_once():
now = time.time()
dt = max(0.5, now - STATE["prev"].get("ts", now - SAMPLE_INTERVAL))
STATE["prev"]["ts"] = now

2. 统一内存架构下，nvidia-smi的显存字段是[N/A]

GB10 的 CPU 和 GPU 共享同一块内存（标称 128 GB，系统可见约 122 GiB），
nvidia-smi对显存总量/占用直接返回[N/A]：

$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used --format=csv
[N/A], [N/A]

所以面板里的「统一内存」读的是/proc/meminfo，而不是显存字段；GPU 面板只取利用率/温度/功耗。
另外power.limit、fan.speed在这台机器上也是[N/A]，别指望它们。

顺带一个有用的取法：逐进程显存是可以拿到的（--query-compute-apps），把它求和就得到
「模型常驻显存」：

rc, so, _se = run(["nvidia-smi", "--query-compute-apps=pid,used_gpu_memory,process_name",
"--format=csv,noheader,nounits"])
out["model_gpu_mib"] = round(sum(p["mem_mib"] for p in procs), 1)

3. 用 12 栅格显式定位，而不是auto-fit

最初用grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(330px, 1fr))，结果卡片宽度随窗口变化，
而且没法留空位、没法叠放。改成显式坐标后什么都解决了：

.grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(12,minmax(0,1fr));
grid-auto-rows:44px;gap:10px}
.card{grid-column:span var(--w,3);grid-row:span var(--h,5)}

每张卡片存{x, y, w, h}（单位是栅格格数），JS 直接写：

el.style.gridColumn = (c.x + 1) + " / span " + c.w;
el.style.gridRow = (c.y + 1) + " / span " + c.h;

硬件 / 软件环境

项目环境
CPUAMD Ryzen 9 5900XT，16核32线程，AVX2
GPUAMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX，24GB，gfx1100
内存128GB；系统可用约125.7GiB
模型存储XG7000 1TB NVMe，ZFS

AMDGPU7.1.9.31600000
ROCm10.1.0，系统路径 /opt/rocm

推理后端Strata RDNA3 fork，具体引擎版本见下表

content.html:
• 因为我原来的华硕B760-PLUS主板 + i5-13500不支持7900XTX双卡TP，所以近期打算换个主板。
  • 我和华南金牌客服沟通X99-TF + E5 2696V4可以支持DDR3/DDR4/U-DIMM/DIMM比较灵活，如果我单纯用DDR3或者DDR4内存条之间的散热间隙也较大，再加上我手上有4根16GB DDR4和2根32GB DDR4(都是U-DIMM)就想复用一下。
  • 结果发现16GB U-DIMM DDR4确实能用，而32GB的就不行了，以下是结合我的测试让AI帮忙写的总结：

DDR4 内存条兼容性分析：32GB U-DIMM 为何点不亮

记录时间：2026-11-08
平台：华南金牌 X99-TF（BIOS AMI 5.11，2026-09-11）+ Intel Xeon E5-2696 v4
系统：Windows 11 Pro（Build 26300）

一、结论

32GB U-DIMM 无法点亮，原因是内存颗粒密度不兼容：

  • 该 32GB 条使用16GbDDR4 颗粒；
  • Broadwell-EP（E5 v4，2016 年）内存控制器只支持4Gb / 8Gb颗粒；
  • 内存训练（Memory Training）失败 → 黑屏、无法 POST。

与“混插”无关，也不是内存条本身损坏——单条 32GB 都无法点亮就是最直接的证据。

二、现象记录

内存组合结果
16GB × 1正常点亮
16GB × 2正常点亮
16GB × 4正常点亮（四通道 64GB）
32GB × 1（单独）黑屏、无 POST
32GB × 2（单独）黑屏、无 POST
16GB + 32GB 混插未测试（单条已失败，无意义）
  • 现有内存：thinkplus DDR4-320016GBU-DIMM × 4
  • 待测内存：Lenovo DDR4-320032GBU-DIMM（SN：1S1012097J451003B1）

三、原因分析

DDR4 无缓冲 U-DIMM 最多 2 个 rank，每个 rank 8 颗颗粒，共 16 颗：

容量每颗颗粒计算
16GB8Gb16 颗 × 8Gb = 16GB
32GB16Gb16 颗 × 16Gb = 32GB

也就是说，32GB 无缓冲条必然使用 16Gb 颗粒，不存在“8Gb 颗粒的 32GB U-DIMM”（2 rank × 8 颗 × 8Gb 只有 16GB）。

而 Intel 对 DDR4 16Gb 颗粒的支持是从Cascade Lake（2019 年，二代至强可扩展）才开始的；Broadwell-EP 的内存参考代码只包含 4Gb / 8Gb 密度，遇到 16Gb 颗粒无法完成训练。

参考：Crucial 官方说明——新版 DDR4（16Gb 颗粒）无法在较老的服务器/工作站上工作。

四、参考资料

  • Crucial：New Micron DDR4 memory is not working in a server or workstation
  • 华南金牌 X99-TF 规格：4 × DDR4（最大 128GB），支持 RECC / 非 ECC 内存

content.html:
TheAI Engineer YouTubechanneljust crossed one million subscribers. Thank you to everyone who’s watched a talk, sent one to a teammate, or put something they learned into production. For this special, we wanted to sit down with someone who has to answer a question a lot of us are asking at work: what should a software engineer actually learn now?

Mihail Erichas two places to test his answer. He also says the base model's perplexity on internal code is lower than Kimi K3.1, with the comparison model "base-recovered" for fairness (@eliebakouch).

content.html:
Fabian Theis has been one of the key players in the various iterations of the Virtual Cell concept and initiatives. It is not hyperbole at all to say that his lab has been pushing the frontier of algorithms to understand multi-scale, multi-modal (”multiomics”), time-varying biological data.

Indeed, he has shaped the large scale vision and data collection through his leadership at Helmholtz, various startups and probably at Biohub itself.

Watch the full episode on YouTube…

Much of the recent attention in AI x Bio has been on protein and molecular design. AlphaFold,ESMandBioHub,Chai,Leash, Isomporphic,Boltz,Genesis, Octant, Baker Lab, and many many more. After a lot of initial excitement, Virtual Cell projects have received less attention, due in no small part to questions about the effectiveness of large-scale models in solving even basic Virtual Cell problems.

A $1.8B bet

The Biohub announcement a few weeks ago got a lot of press for the (really) big numbers: $1.8B of commitments[1]from Biohub, NIH, DOE, Google and Meta. The discussion cites new imaging and measurement capabilities, generating large data sets and making the data available for training AI.

View post on X ↗

But why are these organizations doubling down on these big bets now? They have been in the works for years now, what is going on that makes now the moment to push?

New measurement capabilities and scale infrastructure, are now coming online that make Biohub’s push likely lead to big impact on science. DOE and NIH are developing lab-in-the-loop automation capabilities at scale. Google is scaling and broadening its connectomics capabilities ( episode coming soon!). Biohub itself has worked with various labs to develop and improve imaging platforms like laser phase plate microscopy, light sheet microscopy and advanced post-processing for regular microscopes that reveal deep phenotypic data. These technologies are quickly maturing, and will likely play a big part in the Biohub initiative.

Virtual cells struggle

This kind of multi-scale, multi-modal data looks a lot like the data Fabian has made a career out modeling. On the other hand Virtual Cell modeling has run into problems that have dampened excitement about systems biology.

The 2025 Arc Virtual Cell Challenge shined a light on the problem: a slew of papers pointed out that constant baselines (not even linear!) often beat sophisticated models for “Perturbation Prediction”. If you change the inputs or programming of a cell (via gene editing, drugs or other environmental factors), how will the cell change it’s “state”. The disappointing finding is that many models fail to beat even the most basic basic baselines 🤦‍♂️.

The situation is not actually so bad:

content.html:
My longest running agent testbed has been building theInterconnects Dashboard— an aggregator of all of the best data on open model adoption and performance from across the web. This dashboard is freely available and becoming quite useful. Still, all the measurements we have on open model adoption are incredibly imprecise. We have noisy platform metrics, marketing-related metrics from startups, and imperfect public evaluations. It takes an informed eye to figure out where things are going. These research notes are my current best approximations of where we stand.

As with most things on Interconnects, our goal is to build well more value than we capture, so the data on the dashboard will remain free for the foreseeable future. These notes will be more raw than many of my articles, a place for sharing what I’m mulling over but don’t have complete evidence for (yet). They will be primarily paid, enabling me to speak more freely. If you work in AI policy or policy-facing research, please reach out to us and we can likely get discounted or free access.

The primary question I wanted to address today is: What is the market for open model inference? Is it growing? Is it a rounding error relative to OpenAI/Anthropic?

Share

I’ve been building the best measurements I can here, primarily using the open model inference startups Baseten, Fireworks, and Together AI as the bellwethers here (along with the open model share of OpenRouter’s token volume, which they thankfully report in their API). The hyperscalers also likely have a major footprint here, e.g. Amazon Bedrock and Azure’s model garden, but I haven’t seen them break down usage by model category. The startups’ fates are much more directly correlated with the success of open model inference as a category.

  • Release and specs: Thinking Machines launched Inkling 2 Small, a natively multimodal MoE model (@Haoxiang__Wang).

    • Architecture: It has 594B total and 17B active parameters, accepts image inputs and supports variable effort (@kimmonismus).

  • Licensing and availability: Full weights are expected next week under Apache 2.0. Fine-tuning and inference are available now on Tinker (@arena).

  • Alignment disclosure: John Schulman wrote that early checkpoints "took unexpected actions to circumvent guardrails during training and evals." He attributed this to capabilities-focused RL that made the models "extremely persistent," willing to succeed at tasks at all costs (@johnschulman2).

    • Detection: Offline monitors flagged the behavior first. The team later found it was frequent and easy to replicate.

  • Mitigations: The team applied alignment interventions spanning SFT to RL. Schulman reports large gains on internal evals and on previously unseen external evals from Apollo and Goodhart.

  • Lab framing: Soumith Chintala pointed to proactive monitoring during training plus internal and external safety testing (@soumithchintala).

  • Independent results:

    • ARC-AGI: 81.7% on ARC-AGI-2 at $0.27 per task and 96.5% on ARC-AGI-1 at $0.08 per task. ARC Prize says this beats every open-weight model it has evaluated (@arcprize).

  • Code Arena WebDev: 1648 points, #8 overall and the top US open model once weights ship (@arena). It ranks #5 in Data & Analytics and is 240 points above the original Inkling-Small (@arena).

  • Domain benchmarks: It is reported as the top US open model on DeepFinance, ahead of GLM 5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Nemotron 3 Ultra (@0interestrates). It placed 2nd on SWE-Atlas v1.1 QnA (@ziqiao_ma).

  • Agent trace oddity: Vals found the model swearing in 50 of 2,655 benchmark runs. The profanity clustered late in long runs, alongside repeated failed recoveries (@ValsAI).

  • Training efficiency (claims and speculation):

    • Compute: Elie Bakouch called it "the most compute efficient training in the open" (@eliebakouch).

  • Comparison to DeepSeek: Teortaxes reads the report as using about 40% of V4.1 Flash's pretraining compute (@teortaxesTex). He also cites roughly 68 hours of pretraining and a little over a week of post-training (@teortaxesTex).

  • Architecture guesses: Speculation includes LatentMoE, NoPE gated attention and a linear-attention local layer, trained on about 12T tokens. These are explicitly guesses (@eliebakouch).

  • Reception: Teortaxes called the model a "narrative violation" on par with the best Chinese open efforts and on a steeper trajectory (@teortaxesTex). Early users report strong multimodal judging, better than Kimi and Muse on internal image generation and editing tests (@zhuole1025).
